mt: 'DOLMA DATASET' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE CORPUS AT ITS GRAIN AND PAST THE SAVED ABSTRACT; AI2 NAMED WHERE THE CENSUS NAMES NO INSTITUTION; WHETHER A DOCUMENT KEEPS ITS AUTHOR NOT CARRIED
d: THE CORPUS, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'Dolma is an open-source 3-trillion-token English corpus created by the Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence (Ai2) to support language model pretraining and transparency.' Access (Hugging Face, the GitHub toolkit); key features: scale ('version 1.7 utilizes about 1.715 trillion actual training tokens across ~5.2 billion documents totaling over 5,300 GB'), data sources by kind with their named sets, the curation pipeline ('Bloom filter deduplication (by URL, paragraph, and document), PII/toxicity masking'), licensing ('ODC-BY and Ai2's ImpACT license'), primary use (OLMo); two follow-up questions. Six cards: Hugging Face, the GitHub Pages documentation, Ai2, arXiv, Deep (Learning) Focus, ACL Anthology.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the dataset, the Overview says what it is, who made it and why, where to get it, what it holds, how it was cleaned, under what licences it is released and which models it trains, from the dataset's own pages and its paper.
findings: THE CORPUS AT ITS GRAIN. 'Dolma is an open-source 3-trillion-token English corpus' and 'web content (Common Crawl, C4, RefinedWeb), academic papers (arXiv, Semantic Scholar, peS2o), code (The Stack, StarCoder), public-domain books (Project Gutenberg), encyclopedic material (Wikipedia, Wikibooks), and social media discussions (Reddit, StackExchange)'. The saved abstract: 'a three-trillion-token English corpus, built from a diverse mixture of web content, scientific papers, code, public-domain books, social media, and encyclopedic materials.' The abstract names the six kinds; the composition names a set for each, Project Gutenberg the one source of the books, from the Ai2 card ('Sources: CommonCrawl, C4, peS2o, The Stack, Project Gutenb...').

THE MAKER THE CENSUS DOES NOT HAVE. 'created by the Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence (Ai2)'; three cards carry the same ('Ai2 Dolma: 3 trillion token open corpus for language model pretraining | Ai2'; 'created as training data for OLMo by AI2'). The census row's operator is 'the paper's 36 authors, Luca Soldaini and 35 others', its saved arXiv page reading 'by Luca Soldaini and 35 other authors', and it states that 'the saved sources name no institution', the Hugging Face card having returned HTTP 429 ('We had to rate limit your IP'). The composition names the institution and no author.

A LATER VERSION AND THE LICENCES. 'version 1.7 utilizes about 1.715 trillion actual training tokens across ~5.2 billion documents totaling over 5,300 GB' and 'Released under permissive research licenses (such as ODC-BY and Ai2's ImpACT license)'. The census row's lifecycle: 'later versions or the dataset's current state are unread'. Version 1.7, the document count and the licences are on no saved source; the Ai2 card gives '5,245M documents, 5,334 GB'. The date reaches the composition only on the ACL card ('ACL 2024 Best Resource Paper Award'), agreeing with the abstract's 'Accepted at ACL 2024'; the award is on no saved source.

THE PURPOSE NARROWED TO ONE MODEL FAMILY. The abstract: 'To facilitate scientific research on language model pretraining', against a field where 'commercial models rarely detail their data'. The composition: 'to support language model pretraining and transparency' and 'Designed and used specifically to pre-train the OLMo open-source language model family.' Research drops from the purpose; the openness the abstract argues for stands as 'transparency', and the toolkit as 'the Dolma GitHub Toolkit', agreeing with 'we open-source our data curation toolkit to enable reproduction of our work'.

THE AUTHOR OF A DOCUMENT NOT CARRIED. The census row: 'the saved abstract does not say whether a document in Dolma keeps its author's name, source or attribution metadata', and its reading asks whether a work is carried with 'the metadata that lets it be found and attributed' (#186). The composition's operations on a document are 'language filtering', 'Bloom filter deduplication (by URL, paragraph, and document)' and 'PII/toxicity masking'; nothing in it says what of a book's author or source survives into the corpus, and its follow-up offers 'specific subsets or data processing scripts'.
analysis: The corpus composed accurately and more finely than the saved abstract, from the dataset's own pages, with Ai2 as maker where the census row names only the paper's authors. Whether a document in the corpus keeps its author's name, the census row's open question, is not reached.
